description: Salvaged from the fz-bfh.5.5 spike (the one good reusable piece): a telemetry handler tapping [fz,compiler2,job] SpanStart, counting runs per Job VARIANT, panicking the instant a kind crosses a generous cap -- a fast, deterministic signal NAMING the runaway kind instead of an opaque drive timeout. Land it as a livelock BACKSTOP (generous uniform cap consistent with drive_until_semantic_closure's 10_000), NOT calibrated to tolerate any specific fixture's count -- detecting the subtler demand/analysis over-derivation is fz-bfh.6's tighter, separate measurement. Reusable test-support module; used by world.drive()-based drive-heavy tests.
title: Per-job-kind livelock guard for drive-heavy tests
